chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no breast-feeding after weaning, nor copulation during fasting, nor orphan-hood after puberty, nor silence for a day up to the night, nor conforming to Arab customs after the emigration, nor an emigration after the victory, nor a divorce before the marriage, nor an emancipation before ownership, nor an oath for the son with his father, nor for the slave with his master, nor for the woman with her husband, nor a vow regarding disobedience, nor an oath regarding cutting-off of relationships.'

Thus, the meaning of his words: 'There is no breast-feeding after weaning', is that the child, when it drinks from the milk of the woman after she has weaned him, that breast-feeding would not bring about the prohibition of marriage.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions under which breast-feeding, divorce, or emancipation do not take legal effect in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'la mawdu'a ba'da al-wuqu'' (no effect after occurrence), a cornerstone of Shia jurisprudence for determining the validity of legal acts based on their timing relative to established states. It clarifies that specific conditions, such as breast-feeding, divorce, or emancipation, only produce their intended legal consequences if they occur within the correct temporal or substantive framework, thereby preventing retroactive or premature legal effects.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Mansour Bin Hazim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There is no breast-feeding after weaning, nor copulation during Fasting, nor an orphan-hood after the puberty, nor a silence for a day up to the night, nor conforming to Arab customs after the emigration (Hijra), nor an emigration after the victory (conquest of Makkah), nor a divorce before the marriage, nor an emancipation (of a slave) before ownership, nor a swearing of an oath for the son with his father, nor for the owned slave with his master, nor for the woman with her husband, nor a vow regarding disobedience (to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>), nor a swearing of an oath regarding cutting-off of relationships.

Thus, the Meaning of his<sup>saww</sup> words: ‘There is no breast-feeding after weaning’, is that the child, when it drinks from the milk of the woman after she having weaning him, that breast-feeding would not (bring about a) Prohibition of the marriage’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mansur ibn Yunus from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘

Breastfeeding after weaning is not effective, continuous fasting is not valid, one is not an orphan after experiencing wet-dream, vowing to remain silent for the whole day until the night is not valid, going back to disbelief after migrating to Islam is not permissible, migration after the conquest is not applicable, divorce before marriage is not valid, setting free of slaves before owning a slave is not valid, oath by the son against his father or of a slave against his master, or a wife against her husband is not valid, a vow for unlawful matters is not valid. Swearing to disregard good relation with relatives is not permissible.

The meaning of the words of the Messenger of Allah, ‘Breastfeeding after weaning is not effective’ means that if a boy drinks the milk of a woman after he is weaned, such breastfeeding does not make marriage unlawful.’”
